title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction: Context: in July 1986 Grothendieck is axiomatising 'ateliers' (workshops). An atelier A is a set of 'figures' with three relations. X ⊴ Y is a kind of subordination or inclusion. X ∘≪ Y is a 'well inside' or interior-inclusion relation. X |∘| Y reads as 'interiors disjoint'. The model example is A = Figurations(E), figures in a space E. On the previous page a homomorphism f: A → A' is defined as a map into Â' = A' ⊔ {∅}, i.e. a partial map or pointed-set map. It must preserve the three relations. Conventions are fixed for when a term is ∅: X' ⊴ ∅ always holds, so ⊴ is not an order on Â'. ∅ ∘≪ X' always holds, and X' ∘≪ ∅ holds only if X' = ∅. This page completes the list: c) X' |∘| ∅ is always satisfied. Grothendieck says Â' and these conventions are modelled on the earlier example 2°, presumably a restriction of figurations to a subspace. He then defines Ker f = {X ∈ A | f(X) = ∅}. Condition b) plus the convention 'X' ∘≪ ∅ ⇒ X' = ∅' implies that Ker f is closed downward under ∘≪: if Y ∘≪ X and f(X) = ∅, then f(Y) ∘≪ ∅, so f(Y) = ∅. One would expect kernels to be a distinguished family of subsets (written Σ(A)?). Grothendieck suspects this needs extra conditions on f, but notes it holds in example 2° and its variants. He then asks the converse, a quotient or excision problem. Given N ⊂ A closed under ∘≪, is N the kernel of some homomorphism, and can that homomorphism be chosen canonically? More precisely: is there an atelier A/N ('opérations d'excision') with a universal homomorphism p: A → A/N killing N? The next page states the universal property and the model case. There A = Figurations(E), N = figures with support in E∖E', and A/N = Figurations(E'), viewed as a quotient of A∖N. The aim is to build kernels, quotients and excision for ateliers, analogous to restricting a topological or tame-geometric structure to an open part.
errors: No outright error. Only the ∘≪-convention constrains kernels: with X' ⊴ ∅ and X' |∘| ∅ always true, conditions a) and c) say nothing when f(X) = ∅. Kernels are therefore only forced to be ∘≪-down-closed, which matches Grothendieck's own hedge that more conditions on f are needed. The precise meaning of Σ(A) is not determinable from this page.

ideas.what: Homomorphisms of relational structures as maps into A' ⊔ {∅} (partial maps / pointed sets), with conventions extending the relations to the base point
ideas.modern_name: partial morphisms / pointed-set (Kleisli for Maybe) morphisms of relational structures

ideas.what: Kernel of a homomorphism as the preimage of ∅, shown to be a down-set for the 'well-inside' relation ∘≪
ideas.modern_name: kernel as ideal or sieve for a proximity relation (cf. ideals and round ideals in de Vries/proximity algebras)

ideas.what: Quotient atelier A/N by a ∘≪-closed subset N, universal among homomorphisms killing N, modelled on Figurations(E) → Figurations(E') ('excision')
ideas.modern_name: quotient by an ideal / localisation-restriction to an open part; excision
ideas.usually_credited_to: general universal-algebra quotients; the specific atelier setting is Grothendieck's

missed.claim: Ateliers have relations ⊴ (part-of), ∘≪ (well-inside / non-tangential part) and |∘| (interiors disjoint), with a figure-level rather than point-level viewpoint. This is essentially the signature of region-based topology: mereotopology, contact algebras, de Vries algebras. Kernels and excision quotients here correspond to ideals and relativisation in those theories. Grothendieck's ateliers seem not to be linked to that literature.
missed.quote: Alors b) implique que Ker f ⊂ A est fermé par ∘≪ ... peut-on trouver un atelier A/N (opérations d'excision)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Pointfree and region-based topology (de Vries duality, Boolean contact algebras) could supply ready-made answers to Grothendieck's quotient question. Conversely, his partial-map homomorphisms and excision quotients might give a cleaner categorical treatment there.

missed.claim: Two questions are left open: characterise which ∘≪-closed subsets are kernels, and whether the universal excision quotient A/N exists canonically.
missed.quote: on doit sans doute pour cela imposer des conditions supplémentaires sur f
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is the basic step for any category of ateliers, needed to define exact sequences or excision for a combinatorial tame topology.

deep.surprise_reason: The ateliers programme is itself unpublished and little known, and its affinity with mereotopology and de Vries algebras is an unnoticed link. The page content itself, however, is routine kernel/quotient bookkeeping.
